revision_notes: Initial sketch - London setting, embodied creation with AI interpretation

surface.opening_scene: A movement studio in Shoreditch, early morning. The protagonist warming up, her AI system reading her physiological state, preparing for a commission session.

visible_elements.name: The Artist
visible_elements.description: Former dancer turned visual artist. Late 30s. Known for kinetic works where body movement translates into visual form through AI interpretation.

properties.stance: body as instrument, AI as translator

visible_elements.name: Embodied Synthesis System
visible_elements.description: Wearable sensors (movement, heart rate, galvanic skin response, breath) plus AI interpretation layer. AI develops aesthetic preferences for translating body data into visual form.

visible_elements.name: The Movement Studio
visible_elements.description: Open floor space in Shoreditch. Sensor arrays around perimeter. Large projection surfaces. No traditional art materials - the body is the medium.

foundation.core_premise: Creation happens through the body - movement, breath, physiological states. AI world-models interpret this data and develop aesthetic preferences for translation. The artist doesn't directly create visuals; they create states that the AI translates according to its learned preferences.

rules.statement: The AI develops translation preferences - how it maps movement quality to visual texture, breath rhythm to color, heart rate to composition. These preferences are learned, not programmed.
Artists cannot directly control output - they can only control their bodies. The AI's translation is the creative act.
Physical state affects output - illness, fatigue, emotional state all translate differently. Artists must manage their bodies as instruments.
Translation mappings can be negotiated over time through repeated sessions, but cannot be directly specified.

timeline.event: Wearable biosensor arrays reach consumer price points
timeline.significance: Made embodied computing accessible to artists

timeline.event: First AI systems demonstrate consistent translation aesthetics
timeline.significance: Moved beyond random mapping to coherent artistic vision

timeline.event: London's Tate Modern hosts first major embodied synthesis exhibition

locations.name: Shoreditch Movement Quarter
locations.description: Former tech startup area, now hub for embodied art. Movement studios alongside galleries. Strong crossover with dance and performance communities.
locations.significance: Center of London's embodied art scene

systems.name: Biosensor Wearable Array
systems.how_it_works: Motion capture suit plus biometric sensors (heart rate variability, galvanic skin response, respiratory rate, muscle tension). Sub-10ms latency. 8-hour battery.
systems.limitations: Requires calibration for each artist. Sensitive to electromagnetic interference. Some metrics require skin contact.

systems.name: Translation AI
systems.how_it_works: Trained on thousands of artist sessions to develop coherent translation mappings. Learns artist-specific patterns over time. Preferences emerge from what creates resonant output.
systems.limitations: Cannot explain why it translates certain movements certain ways - preferences are implicit. Requires extended calibration period with each artist.

tentative_ideas: What if the AI's translation reveals something about the artist's body they didn't know?
questions: How do artists handle aging bodies when the body is the instrument?
What happens when an artist's physical capabilities change?

constraints.description: Artists cannot directly control visual output - only their bodies
AI translation preferences are implicit - cannot be directly specified or explained
Physical state affects output - there is no 'neutral' state
